I am an old man now, 76 years, and my eyes and back are not what they used to be. This land here in Shinyanga is dry, and the rains come only once — we have learned to trust cassava and what grows with it, not to waste shillings on fertilizer from town. My sons and their wives help me with the hoeing, and when the weeding gets heavy I call on some young men from the village and pay them with a little money or a share of the harvest. I have no school learning, but I have farmed this soil my whole life, and I do what my father did — plant the cuttings, mix the crops together, and hope the rains are kind.
